To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the participation of peers in the COMPAS programme as co-faciltators with the experts did not increase the effectiveness of the programme.
The experts achieved an increase in knowledge and attitudes towards the HIV and condom use, while experts with peers only succeeded in improving HIV knowledge.
the participation of peers in a programme to promote healthy sexuality in adolescents does not increase its efficacy, when it is delivered by experts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the peer group on the implementation of a programme for the prevention of HIV and STI in adolescents.
the short-term impact of different health agents on the efficacy of a school-based HIV-prevention programme for adolescents in Spain.

the evaluation of the effect on the implementation and effectiveness of a school-based HIV/AIDS prevention programme, the Skills for Adolescents With Healthy Sexuality (COMPAS), which has been developed and tested in Spain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study did not find any evidence to support that the participation of peers in the implementation of a school based HIV prevention programme for Spanish adolescents is more effective than the programme delivered by experts only.

The short-term impact on HIV knowledge and attitudes of a peer-led HIV prevention programme for young adolescents is not significantly greater than the impact of a programme delivered only by experts.
the experts achieved an improvement of HIV knowledge and attitudes, and the experts associated to peers achieved an increase of HIV knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participation of peers as cofacilitators did no increase the efficacy of an HIV prevention program for Spanish adolescents.
the participation of adolescents as co-facilitating agents did not increase the effectiveness of a programme delivered to adolescents by professionals, in the promotion of safer sexual behaviours.
the participation of peers as cofacilitators didnot increase the efficacy of an expert-delivered program to promote healthy sexual behaviors in Spanish adolescents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to have a good facilitator for a programme to work, and that it is important for the facilitator to have a good relationship with the students.
the participation of peers as facilitators does not increase the efficacy for the programme delivered by experts.
the participation of peers in an HIV prevention programme does not increase the efficacy.
